$comment: Each case carries a gold query that was written by hand and verified to
execute. Scoring is execution accuracy: the candidate's result set is
compared to the gold result set, so a query that reaches the right answer by
a different route counts as correct. String-matching SQL would mark correct
answers wrong and is not used.
'skills' records what a case is actually testing, so the error analysis can
say which capability failed rather than only how often something did.
'trap' marks cases where the schema alone leads a model to a plausible wrong
answer - these are the cases the semantic layer exists to fix, and the
difference between the prompt conditions should concentrate here.

cases.question: How many opportunities are in the pipeline in total?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM crm_opportunities

cases.question: How many client accounts are there?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM crm_accounts

cases.question: List the product series and how many products are in each.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT series, COUNT(*) AS n FROM crm_products GROUP BY series ORDER BY series

cases.question: How many opportunities are in each deal stage?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT deal_stage, COUNT(*) AS n FROM crm_opportunities GROUP BY deal_stage ORDER BY deal_stage

cases.question: What is the total value of all won deals?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT SUM(close_value) AS booked FROM crm_opportunities WHERE is_won

cases.question: What is the overall win rate across closed deals?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN is_won THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS win_rate FROM crm_opportunities WHERE is_closed
cases.trap: Computing the rate over all opportunities instead of closed ones counts undecided deals as losses.

cases.question: What is the average value of a won deal?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(close_value) AS avg_won FROM crm_opportunities WHERE is_won
cases.trap: Lost deals carry close_value = 0 rather than NULL, so averaging over all closed deals drags the figure toward zero.

cases.question: What is the win rate for each client sector?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT a.sector, AVG(CASE WHEN o.is_won THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS win_rate FROM crm_opportunities o JOIN crm_accounts a ON a.account = o.account WHERE o.is_closed GROUP BY a.sector ORDER BY a.sector
cases.trap: Needs both the account join and the closed-only filter.

cases.question: Which sales agents booked the most value? Show the top five.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT sales_agent, SUM(close_value) AS booked FROM crm_opportunities WHERE is_won GROUP BY sales_agent ORDER BY booked DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: What is the median sales cycle in days for won deals?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT MEDIAN(cycle_days) AS median_days FROM crm_opportunities WHERE is_won AND cycle_days IS NOT NULL

cases.question: How does booked value break down by regional office?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT t.regional_office, SUM(o.close_value) AS booked FROM crm_opportunities o JOIN crm_sales_teams t ON t.sales_agent = o.sales_agent WHERE o.is_won GROUP BY t.regional_office ORDER BY t.regional_office

cases.question: For each manager, how many agents report to them?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT manager, COUNT(*) AS agents FROM crm_sales_teams GROUP BY manager ORDER BY manager

cases.question: Which products have a list price above 3000?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT product, list_price FROM crm_products WHERE list_price > 3000 ORDER BY list_price DESC

cases.question: What is the median won deal value for each product series?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT p.series, MEDIAN(o.close_value) AS median_value FROM crm_opportunities o JOIN crm_products p ON p.product = o.product WHERE o.is_won GROUP BY p.series ORDER BY p.series

cases.question: How many opportunities have no account recorded?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM crm_opportunities WHERE account IS NULL

cases.question: How many deals closed in each month of 2017?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT strftime(close_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, COUNT(*) AS n FROM crm_opportunities WHERE close_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

cases.question: Which accounts in the technology sector have more than 5000 employees?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT account, employees FROM crm_accounts WHERE sector = 'technology' AND employees > 5000 ORDER BY employees DESC
cases.trap: The source spells this sector 'technolgy'; the cleaned table spells it correctly.

cases.question: What share of opportunities are still open?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN is_closed THEN 0.0 ELSE 1.0 END) AS open_share FROM crm_opportunities

cases.question: How many opportunities did each manager's team close, and how many did they win?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT t.manager, COUNT(*) AS closed, SUM(CASE WHEN o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS won FROM crm_opportunities o JOIN crm_sales_teams t ON t.sales_agent = o.sales_agent WHERE o.is_closed GROUP BY t.manager ORDER BY t.manager

cases.question: Which sector has the highest average won deal value, and what is it?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT a.sector, AVG(o.close_value) AS avg_won FROM crm_opportunities o JOIN crm_accounts a ON a.account = o.account WHERE o.is_won GROUP BY a.sector ORDER BY avg_won DESC LIMIT 1
cases.trap: Averaging close_value over closed rather than won deals includes the zeros lost deals carry.

cases.question: How many accounts are subsidiaries of another company?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM crm_accounts WHERE parent_account IS NOT NULL

cases.question: Compare the median cycle length of won deals against lost deals.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN is_won THEN 'Won' ELSE 'Lost' END AS outcome, MEDIAN(cycle_days) AS median_days FROM crm_opportunities WHERE is_closed AND cycle_days IS NOT NULL GROUP BY outcome ORDER BY outcome

cases.question: What is the total list-price value of the open pipeline?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT SUM(p.list_price) AS open_value FROM crm_opportunities o JOIN crm_products p ON p.product = o.product WHERE NOT o.is_closed
cases.trap: Open deals carry no close_value at all, so the value has to come from the product catalogue.

cases.question: Which five accounts generated the most booked value?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT account, SUM(close_value) AS booked FROM crm_opportunities WHERE is_won AND account IS NOT NULL GROUP BY account ORDER BY booked DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: How many marketing-qualified leads are there?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM funnel_leads

cases.question: How many leads came from each acquisition channel?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT origin AS channel, COUNT(*) AS n FROM funnel_leads GROUP BY origin ORDER BY n DESC

cases.question: How many leads became signed clients?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM deal_outcomes

cases.question: What share of qualified leads converted into signed clients?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM deal_outcomes) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM funnel_leads) AS conversion_rate

cases.question: What share of signed clients ever generated revenue?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN ever_sold THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS attachment_rate FROM deal_outcomes WHERE window_complete
cases.trap: Without the window_complete filter this returns 45.0% instead of 51.4%, because clients signed after the commerce data ends cannot show revenue by construction.

cases.question: What is the median number of days from first contact to signature?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT MEDIAN(days_to_close) AS median_days FROM deal_outcomes

cases.question: How many signed clients are in each business segment? Show the top ten.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT business_segment, COUNT(*) AS n FROM deal_outcomes WHERE business_segment IS NOT NULL GROUP BY business_segment ORDER BY n DESC, business_segment LIMIT 10

cases.question: How much revenue did signed clients generate in their first 90 days, by channel?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT origin AS channel, SUM(revenue_90d) AS revenue FROM deal_outcomes WHERE window_complete GROUP BY origin ORDER BY revenue DESC
cases.trap: Revenue summed without the window filter includes clients with no observation window.

cases.question: How many orders are there in total?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders

cases.question: What is the total item revenue across all non-cancelled orders?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT SUM(i.price) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id WHERE o.order_status <> 'canceled'
cases.trap: Cancelled orders remain in the table and must be excluded from revenue.

cases.question: How many distinct orders contain more than one item line?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM (SELECT order_id FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) t
cases.trap: order_items is one row per line, so counting rows rather than grouping by order gives the wrong answer.

cases.question: What is the average review score?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(review_score) AS avg_score FROM order_reviews

cases.question: How many unique customers are there?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS n FROM customers
cases.trap: customer_id is per order, not per person. Counting it overstates the customer base by 3,345.

cases.question: Which five states have the most delivered orders?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: What share of delivered orders arrived on or before the estimated date?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date <= order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS on_time FROM orders WHERE order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
cases.trap: Orders never delivered must be excluded rather than counted as late.

cases.question: What is the average number of days between purchase and delivery?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(DATE_DIFF('day', order_purchase_timestamp, order_delivered_customer_date)) AS avg_days FROM orders WHERE order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL

cases.question: How many signed clients had a complete 90-day observation window?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM deal_outcomes WHERE window_complete

cases.question: What is the conversion rate from lead to signed client for each channel?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT l.origin AS channel, COUNT(d.mql_id) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS conversion_rate FROM funnel_leads l LEFT JOIN deal_outcomes d ON d.mql_id = l.mql_id GROUP BY l.origin ORDER BY conversion_rate DESC
cases.trap: Needs a LEFT JOIN: an inner join drops channels whose leads never converted and inflates every rate.

cases.question: How many leads had no acquisition channel recorded at all?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM funnel_leads WHERE origin = 'not_recorded'
cases.trap: 'unknown' is a recorded value meaning unidentifiable; 'not_recorded' is the label for a missing one. Merging them conflates two different facts.

cases.question: Which business segments have the highest revenue attachment rate? Show segments with at least twenty clients.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT business_segment, AVG(CASE WHEN ever_sold THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS attachment_rate, COUNT(*) AS clients FROM deal_outcomes WHERE window_complete AND business_segment IS NOT NULL GROUP BY business_segment HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20 ORDER BY attachment_rate DESC

cases.question: What is the total revenue for each seller state? Show the top five.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT s.seller_state, SUM(i.price) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = i.seller_id WHERE o.order_status <> 'canceled' GROUP BY s.seller_state ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: How many orders were cancelled?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'canceled'

cases.question: What is the average review score for each order status?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT o.order_status, AVG(r.review_score) AS avg_score FROM order_reviews r JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = r.order_id GROUP BY o.order_status ORDER BY o.order_status

cases.question: How many signed clients came from each lead type?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT lead_type, COUNT(*) AS n FROM deal_outcomes WHERE lead_type IS NOT NULL GROUP BY lead_type ORDER BY n DESC

cases.question: What is the median 90-day revenue among clients that generated any revenue at all?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT MEDIAN(revenue_90d) AS median_revenue FROM deal_outcomes WHERE window_complete AND revenue_90d > 0
cases.trap: The median across all clients is zero, because most bill nothing in 90 days.

cases.question: How many products are there in each English category? Show the top ten.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT product_category_name_english, COUNT(*) AS n FROM products WHERE product_category_name_english IS NOT NULL GROUP BY product_category_name_english ORDER BY n DESC, product_category_name_english LIMIT 10

cases.question: How many leads were first contacted in each month?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT strftime(first_contact_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, COUNT(*) AS n FROM funnel_leads GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

cases.question: Which sellers have the highest lifetime revenue? Show the top five with their average review score.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT seller_id, revenue_brl, avg_review_score FROM seller_performance ORDER BY revenue_brl DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: What is the average order value, counting each order once?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(order_total) AS avg_order_value FROM (SELECT i.order_id, SUM(i.price) AS order_total FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id WHERE o.order_status <> 'canceled' GROUP BY i.order_id) t
cases.trap: Averaging item price gives the average line value, not the average order value. The order has to be aggregated first.

cases.question: How many signed clients generated no revenue at all within their first 90 days?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM deal_outcomes WHERE window_complete AND revenue_90d = 0

cases.question: Which landing pages produced the most leads? Show the top five.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT landing_page_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM funnel_leads GROUP BY landing_page_id ORDER BY n DESC, landing_page_id LIMIT 5

cases.question: What is the average time to close for each business type?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT business_type, AVG(days_to_close) AS avg_days FROM deal_outcomes WHERE business_type IS NOT NULL GROUP BY business_type ORDER BY business_type

cases.question: How many orders had a review score of 1?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS n FROM order_reviews WHERE review_score = 1
cases.trap: review_id is not unique across orders, so counting reviews rather than distinct orders can miscount.

cases.question: For clients with a complete window, what is the average revenue in the first 90 days by lead type?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT lead_type, AVG(revenue_90d) AS avg_revenue FROM deal_outcomes WHERE window_complete AND lead_type IS NOT NULL GROUP BY lead_type ORDER BY avg_revenue DESC

cases.question: How many distinct sellers appear in the order items?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) AS n FROM order_items

cases.question: Which five business segments produced the most 90-day revenue in total?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT business_segment, SUM(revenue_90d) AS revenue FROM deal_outcomes WHERE window_complete AND business_segment IS NOT NULL GROUP BY business_segment ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: What is the average freight cost per item line?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(freight_value) AS avg_freight FROM order_items

cases.question: How many clients signed in each month?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT strftime(won_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, COUNT(*) AS n FROM deal_outcomes GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

cases.question: Which customer states have an average delivery time above 20 days? Include only states with at least 500 delivered orders.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_state, AVG(DATE_DIFF('day', o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_delivered_customer_date)) AS avg_days FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_state HAVING COUNT(*) >= 500 AND AVG(DATE_DIFF('day', o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_delivered_customer_date)) > 20 ORDER BY avg_days DESC

cases.question: What proportion of signed clients came from paid search?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN origin = 'paid_search' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS share FROM deal_outcomes

cases.question: How many item lines are there per order on average?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS avg_lines FROM order_items

cases.question: Which five sellers received the most reviews?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT seller_id, reviews FROM seller_performance WHERE reviews IS NOT NULL ORDER BY reviews DESC, seller_id LIMIT 5

cases.question: What is the revenue attachment rate for each acquisition channel, restricted to clients with a complete window?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT origin AS channel, AVG(CASE WHEN ever_sold THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS attachment_rate, COUNT(*) AS clients FROM deal_outcomes WHERE window_complete GROUP BY origin ORDER BY attachment_rate DESC

cases.question: How many orders are there for each order status?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT order_status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY order_status ORDER BY n DESC

cases.question: What is the total 90-day revenue across all clients with a complete window?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT SUM(revenue_90d) AS revenue FROM deal_outcomes WHERE window_complete

cases.question: Which behaviour profile is most common among signed clients?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT behaviour_primary, COUNT(*) AS n FROM deal_outcomes WHERE behaviour_primary IS NOT NULL GROUP BY behaviour_primary ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: How many sellers have an average review score below 3?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM seller_performance WHERE avg_review_score < 3

cases.question: What is the longest time to close recorded for any signed client?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT MAX(days_to_close) AS max_days FROM deal_outcomes
